questions.q: What does Cascade Foodservice Equipment Co. sell, and to whom?
options: Consumer kitchen appliances sold directly to home cooks online
Commercial kitchen equipment sold B2B to restaurants, hotels, healthcare/institutional kitchens, schools, and caterers
Software for restaurant point-of-sale systems
Raw food ingredients sold to grocery distributors
questions.explain: The lesson defines Cascade as a B2B seller of commercial kitchen equipment -- ranges, ovens, coolers, dishwashing systems, and hoods -- to restaurants, hotels, healthcare/institutional kitchens, schools, and caterers.

questions.q: Put Cascade's Opportunity stages in the correct order.
options: Needs Analysis, Qualifying, Negotiation/Review, Equipment Proposal, Closed Won
Equipment Proposal, Qualifying, Closed Won, Needs Analysis, Negotiation/Review
Qualifying, Needs Analysis, Equipment Proposal, Negotiation/Review, Closed Won/Lost
Closed Won, Qualifying, Needs Analysis, Negotiation/Review, Equipment Proposal
questions.explain: The lesson lists the five open stages in order: Qualifying, Needs Analysis, Equipment Proposal, Negotiation/Review, ending in Closed Won or Closed Lost.

questions.q: At Cascade, who owns the large, multi-location Key Accounts, and who manages the New Business sales team?
options: Angela Wu owns Key Accounts; Marcus Webb manages New Business
Priya Nair owns Key Accounts; Derek Oyelaran manages New Business
Monica Reyes owns Key Accounts; Jordan Kessler manages New Business
Tom Baptiste owns Key Accounts; Priya Nair manages New Business
questions.explain: The lesson states Priya Nair is the Senior Account Executive who owns Cascade's largest Key Accounts, while Derek Oyelaran manages the New Business team.

questions.q: What two business realities at Cascade become the two custom objects built in Lesson 9?
options: Employee payroll and office supply ordering
Trade show attendance and website traffic analytics
Executive compensation and annual budgeting
An installation's own post-sale lifecycle, and recurring service contracts independent of any one Opportunity
questions.explain: The lesson explains that an installation has its own lifecycle after a deal closes, and many customers pay separately for ongoing maintenance through a recurring service contract -- neither fits the standard objects, which is why they become custom objects.

questions.q: Why does this lesson repeat that Cascade Foodservice Equipment Co. is fictional?
options: To make clear it's an illustrative scenario for practice, not a real business or case study, consistent with how this catalog handles invented capstone scenarios
Because the course will later reveal it is based on a real company
Because fictional companies are required by Salesforce's terms of service
Because the name was legally trademarked by another organization
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states, more than once, that Cascade is fictional and illustrative, invented purely to give this capstone one consistent, concrete scenario to build around.
